title: fatboi fitness v2
author: Joshua J.
desc:
# Fatboi Fitness V2 — Upper Body Specialization / Recomp Block

## Program Goal

This is an upper-body hypertrophy specialization program designed around:

* rebuilding muscle and movement quality during a recomp/cutting phase,
* improving chest mechanics and recruitment,
* emphasizing shoulder width and upper-back density,
* maintaining lower body strength and muscle,
* and building work capacity for future athletic and martial arts goals.

This is NOT:

* a maximal strength peaking program,
* a powerlifting program,
* or a “destroy yourself every session” program.

The goal is:

> high-quality recoverable volume with long-term progression.

---

# Program Philosophy

This program is built around:

* moderate-to-high frequency,
* moderate-to-high recoverable volume,
* technique refinement,
* and intelligent fatigue distribution.

The emphasis is:

* chest,
* shoulders,
* upper back,
* and arms.

Lower body is currently maintained with enough work to preserve strength, muscle, and movement quality while bodyweight decreases and recovery improves.

Future blocks may rotate emphasis toward:

* legs,
* lower back,
* posterior chain,
* deadlift strength,
* front squats,
* and athletic performance.

---

# Progression Model

## Main Progression Lifts

The primary compounds use a 3-week volume wave progression.

### Example:

Week 1:
3 working sets

Week 2:
4 working sets

Week 3:
5 working sets

Week 4:
Deload (~50–60% volume)

Then:

* increase load slightly,
* restart at Week 1 volume,
* and repeat.

The goal is:

> own the weight before increasing the weight.

This progression style builds:

* technique,
* work capacity,
* hypertrophy,
* and stable long-term progress.

---

# Primary Progression Exercises

## Chest

* Incline Bench Press
* Flat Bench Press

Each pressing movement has its own priority day.

## Upper Back

* T-Bar Row

## Shoulders

* Main Shoulder Press Variation

## Posterior Chain

* Romanian Deadlift

---

# Stable Accessories

Accessories generally remain at stable set counts and progress through:

* execution,
* control,
* MMC,
* reps,
* and occasional load increases.

These are NOT intended to endlessly accumulate sets.

Examples:
* lateral raises,
* rear delt work,
* pec deck,
* pulldowns,
* curls,
* pushdowns,
* face pulls.

wave intensity of OHP and Pendlay row by pyramid set, 2 practice sets then working sets then back off sets removing backoff and/or ramp up sets as working sets increases.

EX. week 1 2PS 3 WS 2BOS week 2 2PS 4WS 1BOS, week 3 0-1 PS 5WS 0BOS week 4 deload completely. only these 2 do not do with any other movement, only added to not have to restructure program so that upper back and shoulders get the technical touch that presses do without trying to shove another session in.
